title: Deep learning architectures: convolution, recurrence and attention
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the architectures behind modern deep learning: convolution and pooling, convolutional networks from LeNet to ResNet, recurrent networks, LSTMs and GRUs, sequence-to-sequence models, attention, the transformer, embeddings and positional encodings, graph neural networks, self-supervised and contrastive learning, and transfer learning and fine-tuning.

weeks.2: Convolutional networks: from LeNet to ResNet
weeks.3: Recurrent networks and backpropagation through time
weeks.7: The transformer: self-attention, multiple heads and feed-forward blocks
weeks.9: Graph neural networks and message passing
weeks.12: Choosing an architecture for a problem

blocks.deliverable: Compute convolutions and output shapes for a small network by hand and in code.
Run a recurrent cell over a short sequence by hand.
Compute attention weights and outputs for a small set of queries and keys.
Week 7 midterm; trace one transformer block on a tiny input.
Run one round of message passing on a small graph.
Write a design memo choosing an architecture for three tasks.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Tiny transformer: implement scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, a transformer block with layer normalization and positional encodings, train a very small model on a supplied character-level toy task (such as reversing short strings) with plain Python or any framework on your own computer, and write a report on what the attention weights show and how accuracy changes with model size.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
